四年正月…是月二十三日

units.zh: 張全義，字國維，濮州臨濮人。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi, whose courtesy name was Guowei, came from Linpu in Puzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, styled Guowei, was a native of Linpu in Puzhou.

units.zh: 初名居言，賜名全義，梁祖改為宗奭；
units.en: He was originally named Juyan, was granted the name Quanyi, and the Liang Founder renamed him Zongyi;
units.literal: His original name was Juyan; he was granted the name Quanyi; the Founder of Liang changed it to Zongyi;

units.zh: 莊宗定河南，復名全義。
units.en: After Emperor Zhuangzong secured Henan, his name was restored to Quanyi.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan, he was again named Quanyi.

units.zh: 祖璉，父誠，世為田農。
units.en: His grandfather Lian and his father Cheng had been farmers for generations.
units.literal: His grandfather was Lian, his father Cheng; for generations they were field farmers.

units.zh: 全義為縣嗇夫，嘗為令所辱。
units.en: Quanyi worked as a county grain clerk and had once been humiliated by the local magistrate.
units.literal: Quanyi served as a district grain clerk and was once humiliated by the magistrate.

units.zh: 乾符末，黃巢起冤句，全義亡命入巢軍。
units.en: When Huang Chao rebelled at Yuanqu in the final years of Qianfu, Quanyi fled and joined his forces.
units.literal: At the end of the Qianfu era, Huang Chao rose at Yuanqu; Quanyi fled for his life and entered Chao's army.

units.zh: 巢入長安，以全義為吏部尚書，充水運使。
units.en: After Chao took Chang'an, he made Quanyi Minister of the Civil Office and Superintendent of Water Transport.
units.literal: When Chao entered Chang'an, he appointed Quanyi Minister of the Civil Office and made him Water Transport Commissioner.

units.zh: 巢敗，依諸葛爽於河陽，累遷至裨校，屢有戰功，爽表為澤州刺史。
units.en: When Chao fell, Quanyi attached himself to Zhuge Shuang at Heyang, rose through the ranks to junior officer with repeated distinctions in battle, and Shuang recommended him as prefect of Zezhou.
units.literal: When Chao was defeated, he joined Zhuge Shuang at Heyang; he was repeatedly promoted to junior officer, had repeated battle achievements, and Shuang memorialized for him to be Prefect of Zezhou.

units.zh: 光啟初，爽卒，其子仲方為留後。
units.en: Early in Guangqi, Shuang died and his son Zhongfang took over as acting governor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Shuang died; his son Zhongfang became acting military governor.

units.zh: 部將劉經與李罕之爭據洛陽，罕之敗經於聖善寺，乘勝欲攻河陽，營於洛口。
units.en: Subordinate Liu Jing and Li Hanzhi fought over Luoyang; Hanzhi defeated Liu at Shengshan Temple and, pressing his advantage, moved to attack Heyang, encamping at Luokou.
units.literal: The subordinate general Liu Jing and Li Hanzhi contested possession of Luoyang; Hanzhi defeated Jing at Shengshan Temple; seizing victory, he wished to attack Heyang and encamped at Luokou.

units.zh: 經遣全義拒之，全義乃與罕之同盟結義，返攻經於河陽，為經所敗，收合餘眾，與罕之據懷州，乞師於武皇。
units.en: Liu sent Quanyi to oppose him, but Quanyi instead allied with Hanzhi and turned on Liu at Heyang; defeated, he regrouped, joined Hanzhi in holding Huaizhou, and sought aid from the Martial Emperor.
units.literal: Jing dispatched Quanyi to resist him; Quanyi then formed a sworn alliance with Hanzhi, returned to attack Jing at Heyang, was defeated by Jing, gathered his remaining troops, and with Hanzhi held Huaizhou, begging troops from the Martial Emperor.

units.zh: 武皇遣澤州刺史安金俊助之，進攻河陽，劉經、仲方委城奔汴，罕之遂自領河陽，表全義為河南尹。
units.en: The Martial Emperor sent An Jinjun, prefect of Zezhou, to help; they attacked Heyang; Liu and Zhongfang abandoned the city for Bian; Hanzhi took Heyang himself and recommended Quanyi as Intendant of Henan.
units.literal: The Martial Emperor sent the prefect of Zezhou An Jinjun to assist them; they advanced to attack Heyang; Liu Jing and Zhongfang abandoned the city and fled to Bian; Hanzhi then himself took over Heyang and memorialized Quanyi as Intendant of Henan.

units.zh: 全義性勤儉，善撫軍民，雖賊寇充斥，而勸耕務農，由是倉儲殷積。
units.en: By nature industrious and frugal, Quanyi excelled at governing soldiers and civilians alike; despite banditry everywhere, he promoted farming, and his storehouses grew full.
units.literal: Quanyi by nature was diligent and frugal, good at comforting army and people; although bandits filled the land, he urged farming and devoted himself to agriculture, whereby granaries became abundantly stocked.

units.zh: 〈（王始至洛，於麾下百人中，選可使者一十八人，命之曰屯將。
units.en: (When the Prince first came to Luoyang, he picked eighteen capable men from his hundred followers and appointed them Garrison Commanders.
units.literal: (When the Prince first arrived at Luoyang, from among a hundred men under his command he selected eighteen who could be sent on missions and named them Garrison Commanders.

units.zh: 每人給旗一口，榜一道，於舊十八縣中，令招農戶，令自耕種，流民漸歸。
units.en: Each received a banner and a proclamation; across the old eighteen counties they were to recruit farmers and let them till the land themselves, and refugees gradually came back.
units.literal: Each was given one banner and one placard; in the former eighteen counties he ordered them to recruit farming households and have them cultivate on their own; displaced people gradually returned.

units.zh: 王於百人中，又選可使者十八人，命之曰屯副，民之來者撫綏之，除殺人者死，餘但加杖而已，無重刑，無租稅，流民之歸漸眾。
units.en: From the same hundred men he chose eighteen more as Garrison Deputies to settle newcomers; only murderers were executed, all other offenses meriting no more than a beating; there were no harsh penalties and no taxes, and the returning population swelled.
units.literal: From among the hundred men the Prince again selected eighteen who could be sent and named them Garrison Deputies; those among the people who came were comforted and pacified; except for murderers, who were put to death, the rest received only beating; there were no heavy punishments and no rent or tax; returning displaced people gradually grew numerous.

units.zh: 王又於麾下選書計一十八人，命之曰屯判官。
units.en: He also chose eighteen clerks from his staff and made them Garrison Administrative Officers.
units.literal: The Prince again selected eighteen clerks and accountants from his followers and named them Garrison Administrative Officers.

units.zh: 不一二年，十八屯中每屯戶至數千。
units.en: Within a year or two, each of the eighteen garrisons had several thousand households.
units.literal: In no more than a year or two, in each of the eighteen garrisons households reached several thousand.

units.zh: 王命農隙，每選丁夫授以弓矢槍劍，為坐作進退之法。
units.en: During the farming off-season he selected able-bodied men, armed them with bows, arrows, spears, and swords, and drilled them in formation movements.
units.literal: In the agricultural slack season the Prince ordered that able-bodied men be selected and given bows, arrows, spears, and swords, and taught methods of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating.

units.zh: 行之一二年，每屯增戶。
units.en: After a year or two of this practice, every garrison gained more households.
units.literal: After carrying this out for a year or two, each garrison increased its households.

units.zh: 大者六七千，次者四千，下之二三千，共得丁夫閑弓矢、槍劍者二萬餘人。
units.en: The largest garrisons had six or seven thousand people, the middling ones four thousand, the smallest two or three thousand; altogether more than twenty thousand men stood ready with bows, arrows, spears, and swords.
units.literal: The largest had six or seven thousand, the next four thousand, the smallest two or three thousand; in all there were more than twenty thousand able-bodied men at leisure with bows, arrows, spears, and swords.

units.zh: 有賊盜即時擒捕之，刑寬事簡，遠近歸之如市。
units.en: Bandits were captured on the spot; with lenient law and light administration, people flocked in from far and near as to a market.
units.literal: When there were bandits they were immediately seized; punishments were lenient and affairs simple; from near and far people came to join as if to a market.

units.zh: 五年之內，號為富庶，於是奏每縣除令簿主之。）〉
units.en: Within five years the region was accounted prosperous, and he then memorialized that each county should have a magistrate and clerks appointed to govern it.)〉
units.literal: Within five years it was called prosperous; thereupon he memorialized that in each county a magistrate and clerks be appointed to govern.)〉

units.zh: 罕之貪暴不法，軍中乏食，每取給於全義。
units.en: Hanzhi was greedy and brutal; his troops were short of food and constantly drew supplies from Quanyi.
units.literal: Hanzhi was greedy, violent, and lawless; the army lacked food and constantly took supplies from Quanyi.

units.zh: 二人初相得甚歡，而至是求取無厭，動加淩轢，全義苦之。
units.en: They had begun on excellent terms, but now Hanzhi's demands were endless and his bullying constant, and Quanyi was worn down by it.
units.literal: At first the two men got along very well, but by this time his demands were insatiable and he constantly added insult and oppression; Quanyi suffered from it.

units.zh: 文德元年四月，罕之出軍寇晉、絳，全義乘其無備，潛兵襲取河陽，全義乃兼領河陽節度。
units.en: In the fourth month of Wende 1, Hanzhi marched out to raid Jin and Jiang; Quanyi struck while he was unprepared, seized Heyang by surprise, and took the Heyang command as well.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Wende, Hanzhi led troops out to raid Jin and Jiang; Quanyi took advantage of his being unprepared and with hidden troops seized Heyang; Quanyi then concurrently held the Heyang military governorship.

units.zh: 〈（《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》云：罕之鎮三城，知王專以教民耕織為務，常宣言於眾曰：「田舍翁何足憚。」
units.en: (According to 《Old Tales of Luoyang Gentry》, Hanzhi held the Three Cities and knew the Prince cared only for teaching farming and weaving; he would tell his men, "What is there to fear from a country bumpkin."
units.literal: (《Old Tales of Luoyang Gentry》 says: Hanzhi governed the Three Cities and knew the Prince devoted himself solely to teaching the people farming and weaving; he often proclaimed to the crowd: "What is there to fear from a rustic farmer."

units.zh: 王聞之，蔑如也。
units.en: The Prince heard this and paid it no heed.
units.literal: When the Prince heard it, he treated it with contempt.

units.zh: 每飛尺書於王，求軍食及縑帛，王曰：「李太傅所要，不得不奉之。」
units.en: Whenever Hanzhi sent urgent demands for provisions and silk, the Prince would say, "Whatever Grand Mentor Li wants, we must provide it."
units.literal: Whenever he sent urgent letters to the Prince demanding army provisions and silk cloth, the Prince said: "Whatever Grand Mentor Li wants, we cannot but supply it."

units.zh: 左右及賓席咸以為不可與，王曰：「第與之。」
units.en: His attendants and guests all objected, but the Prince said, "Give it to him anyway."
units.literal: Those at his side and among his guests all thought it should not be given, but the Prince said: "Just give it to him."

units.zh: 似若畏之者，左右不曉。
units.en: He seemed to be afraid of Hanzhi, and his men could not fathom why.
units.literal: As if he feared him; those at his side did not understand.

units.zh: 罕之謂王畏己，不設備。
units.en: Hanzhi concluded the Prince feared him and let his guard down.
units.literal: Hanzhi thought the Prince feared him and made no preparations.

units.zh: 因罕之舉兵收懷、澤，王乃密召屯兵，潛師夜發，遲明入三城。
units.en: When Hanzhi marched out to recover Huai and Ze, the Prince secretly mobilized his garrison troops, marched by night, and at dawn took the Three Cities.
units.literal: Because Hanzhi raised troops to recover Huai and Ze, the Prince secretly summoned the garrison troops, sent hidden forces out by night, and at dawn entered the Three Cities.

units.zh: 罕之乃逃遁投河東，朝廷即授王兼鎮三城。）〉
units.en: Hanzhi fled to Hedong, and the court promptly gave the Prince concurrent command of all three cities.)〉
units.literal: Hanzhi then fled and threw himself on Hedong; the court immediately appointed the Prince to govern the Three Cities concurrently.)〉

units.zh: 罕之求援於武皇，武皇復遣兵助攻河陽，會汴人救至而退。
units.en: Hanzhi appealed to the Martial Emperor, who sent troops to help retake Heyang, but they withdrew when Bian reinforcements arrived.
units.literal: Hanzhi sought aid from the Martial Emperor; the Martial Emperor again sent troops to assist in attacking Heyang; when men from Bian arrived to rescue them they withdrew.

units.zh: 梁祖以丁會守河陽，全義復為河南尹、檢校司空。
units.en: The Liang Founder put Ding Hui in charge of Heyang, and Quanyi was restored as Intendant of Henan and Acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: The Founder of Liang had Ding Hui guard Heyang; Quanyi again became Intendant of Henan and Acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 全義感梁祖援助之恩，自是依附，皆從其制。
units.en: Grateful for the Liang Founder's support, Quanyi from then on submitted to him in all things.
units.literal: Quanyi was moved by the Founder's grace in aiding him; from then on he attached himself and followed all his orders.

units.zh: 初，蔡賊孫儒、諸葛爽爭據洛陽，迭相攻伐，七八年間，都城灰燼，滿目荊榛。
units.en: Earlier, the Cai rebel Sun Ru and Zhuge Shuang had fought over Luoyang for seven or eight years until the capital lay in ashes and brambles covered the land.
units.literal: Earlier, the Cai bandit Sun Ru and Zhuge Shuang had contested possession of Luoyang, attacking each other in turn; for seven or eight years the capital was ashes, the eye meeting only brambles and thorns.

units.zh: 全義初至，惟與部下聚居故市，井邑窮民，不滿百戶。
units.en: When Quanyi first arrived, he and his men settled in the old market district among fewer than a hundred destitute households.
units.literal: When Quanyi first arrived, he and his subordinates dwelt together only in the old market quarter; the wells and hamlets had destitute people numbering fewer than a hundred households.

units.zh: 全義善於撫納，課部人披榛種藝，且耕且戰，以粟易牛，歲滋墾辟，招復流散，待之如子。
units.en: Skilled at winning people over, he had his men clear the brambles and plant crops, farming between battles and trading grain for oxen; each year brought more land under cultivation, and he drew back the displaced and treated them like his own children.
units.literal: Quanyi was good at comforting and accepting people; he ordered his subordinates to clear brambles and plant crops, farming while fighting, exchanging grain for oxen; year by year reclaimed land increased; he recruited back the scattered and treated them like sons.

units.zh: 每農祥勸耕之始，全義必自立畎畝，餉以酒食，政寬事簡，吏不敢欺。
units.en: At the start of each planting season he worked the fields himself and feasted the farmers; with lenient rule and simple administration, his officials dared not cheat.
units.literal: At the beginning of each agricultural season when farming was urged, Quanyi always himself stood in the furrows and fields and provided wine and food; government was lenient and affairs simple, and clerks did not dare deceive.

units.zh: 數年之間，京畿無閑田，編戶五六萬。
units.en: Within a few years no land around the capital lay fallow, and registered households numbered fifty or sixty thousand.
units.literal: Within several years there was no idle land in the capital region; registered households reached fifty or sixty thousand.

units.zh: 乃築壘於故市，建置府署，以防外寇。
units.en: He then built fortifications in the old market, set up government offices, and defended against outside raiders.
units.literal: He then built ramparts in the old market, established government offices, and guarded against outside raiders.

units.zh: 〈（《洛陽縉紳舊聞記》：王每喜民力耕織者，某家今年蠶麥善，去都城一舍之內，必馬足及之，悉召其家老幼，親慰勞之，賜以酒食茶彩，丈夫遺之布褲，婦人裙衫，時民間尚衣青，婦人皆青絹為之。
units.en: (《Old Tales of Luoyang Gentry》 records that whenever a household excelled at farming and weaving, if their silkworms and wheat were good that year and they lived within a day's ride of the capital, he would go in person, summon the whole family, comfort them, and give wine, food, tea, and gifts—trousers for the men, skirts for the women, all in the blue silk the people then favored.
units.literal: (《Old Tales of Luoyang Gentry》: Whenever the Prince was pleased with a household's farming and weaving, if some family that year had good silkworms and wheat within one she (a day's journey) of the capital, he would certainly ride there on horseback, summon all the old and young of that family, personally comfort and encourage them, and bestow wine, food, tea, and colored goods; to the men he gave cloth trousers, to the women skirts and jackets; at the time the common people still favored blue clothing, and the women all had theirs made of blue silk.

units.zh: 取其新麥新繭，對之喜動顏色，民間有竊言者曰：「大王見好聲妓，等閑不笑，惟見好蠶麥即笑爾。」
units.en: Presented with fresh wheat and cocoons, his face lit up with joy; people whispered, "The Prince never smiles for fine entertainers, but good silkworms and wheat always make him smile."
units.literal: Taking their new wheat and new cocoons, facing them his pleasure moved his countenance; among the people some whispered: "When the Great Prince sees good singing girls he ordinarily does not smile; only when he sees good silkworms and wheat does he smile."

units.zh: 其真樸皆此類。
units.en: Such was his unaffected nature in every respect.
units.literal: His genuineness and simplicity were all of this kind.

units.zh: 每觀秋稼，見田中無草者，必下馬命賓客觀之，召田主慰勞之，賜之衣物。
units.en: When inspecting the autumn harvest, if he saw a weedless field he would dismount with his guests to admire it, summon the farmer, praise him, and give him clothes.
units.literal: Whenever he viewed the autumn crops, if he saw fields with no weeds he would certainly dismount and order his guests to observe, summon the field owner, comfort and encourage him, and bestow clothing.

units.zh: 若見禾中有草，地耕不熟，立召田主集眾決責之。
units.en: If he found weeds in the grain or poorly tilled soil, he would summon the farmer at once and have the neighbors decide his punishment.
units.literal: If he saw weeds among the grain or land poorly tilled, he immediately summoned the field owner, gathered the crowd, and adjudicated punishment.

units.zh: 若苗荒地生，詰之，民訴以牛疲或闕人耕鋤，則田邊下馬，立召其鄰仵責之曰：「此少人牛，何不眾助之。」
units.en: If crops grew on neglected land, he questioned why; when farmers said their oxen were worn out or labor was short, he would dismount at the field edge, call the neighbors together, and scold them: "This household lacks oxen and hands—why haven't you all helped."
units.literal: If he saw seedlings growing in wasteland he questioned it; when the people pleaded that oxen were exhausted or men for hoeing were lacking, he dismounted at the field edge, immediately summoned the neighboring households, and reproached them: "Here men and oxen are few—why do you not all help."

units.zh: 鄰仵皆伏罪，即赦之。
units.en: The neighbors would confess and be forgiven at once.
units.literal: The neighboring households all confessed guilt and were immediately pardoned.

units.zh: 自是洛陽之民無遠近，民之少牛者相率助之，少人者亦然。
units.en: After that, throughout Luoyang, households short of oxen or labor helped one another by common agreement.
units.literal: From then on among the people of Luoyang, near and far, those with few oxen aided one another in groups, and those with few men did likewise.

units.zh: 田夫田婦，相勸以耕桑為務，是以家有蓄積，水旱無饑民。
units.en: Farmers and their wives urged one another to devote themselves to agriculture and sericulture, so that every household had reserves and no one went hungry in flood or drought.
units.literal: Farmers and farm wives urged one another to make farming and sericulture their task; thus every household had stores, and in flood or drought there were no starving people.

units.zh: 王誠信，每水旱祈祭，必具湯沐，素食別寢，至祠祭所，儼然若對至尊，容如不足。
units.en: Deeply devout, whenever he prayed in drought or flood he bathed, ate vegetarian food in a separate room, and at the shrine conducted himself with the solemnity due a sovereign, humble in every gesture.
units.literal: The Prince was sincere in faith; whenever he prayed in drought or flood he always prepared bathing, ate vegetarian food in a separate chamber, and at the shrine was solemn as if facing the supreme lord, his bearing as if insufficient.

units.zh: 遇旱，祈禱未雨，左右必曰：「王可開塔」，即無畏師塔也，在龍門廣化寺。
units.en: In drought, before rain came his attendants would say, "Your Highness should open the pagoda"—meaning the pagoda of Master Wuwei at Guanghua Temple on Longmen.
units.literal: When drought came, before rain fell from prayer those at his side always said: "Your Highness can open the pagoda"—that is, the pagoda of Master Wuwei, at Longmen Guanghua Temple.

units.zh: 王即依言而開塔，未嘗不澍雨，故當時俚諺云：「王禱雨，買雨具。」）〉
units.en: He would open it as advised, and rain invariably followed; hence the saying, "When the Prince prays for rain, buy yourself an umbrella.")〉
units.literal: The Prince then followed their words and opened the pagoda; rain never failed to pour; thus the popular saying of the time ran: "When the Prince prays for rain, go buy rain gear.")〉

units.zh: 梁祖迫昭宗東遷，命全義繕治洛陽宮城，累年方集。
units.en: When the Liang Founder compelled Emperor Zhaozong to move east, he ordered Quanyi to restore the Luoyang palace, a task that took years to complete.
units.literal: The Founder of Liang forced Emperor Zhaozong to move east and ordered Quanyi to repair the Luoyang palace city; only after many years was it completed.

units.zh: 昭宗至洛陽，梁祖將圖禪代，慮全義心有異同，乃以判官韋震為河南尹，遂移全義為天平軍節度使、守中書令、東平王。
units.en: When Zhaozong reached Luoyang, the Founder planned his takeover and feared Quanyi's loyalty; he replaced him with his aide Wei Zhen as Intendant of Henan and moved Quanyi to the Tianping command as Guardian Minister of the Central Secretariat and Prince of Dongping.
units.literal: When Zhaozong arrived at Luoyang, the Founder planned to seize the throne by abdication and feared Quanyi might differ in mind; he therefore made his aide Wei Zhen Intendant of Henan and transferred Quanyi to be military governor of Tianping, Guardian Minister of the Central Secretariat, and Prince of Dongping.

units.zh: 〈（《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》：齊王與梁祖互為中書令、尚書令，及梁祖兼四鎮，齊王累表讓兼鎮，蓋潛識梁祖奸雄，避其權位，欲圖自全之計。
units.en: (《Old Tales of Luoyang Gentry》 notes that the Prince of Qi and the Liang Founder had each served as Minister of the Central Secretariat and Minister of the Imperial Secretariat; when the Founder took four commands concurrently, the Prince repeatedly asked to yield his concurrent posts, having sensed the Founder's ambition and seeking to keep himself safe.
units.literal: (《Old Tales of Luoyang Gentry》: The Prince of Qi and the Founder of Liang were each Minister of the Central Secretariat and Minister of the Imperial Secretariat; when the Founder concurrently held four commands, the Prince of Qi repeatedly memorialized to yield the concurrent commands, secretly recognizing the Founder's treacherous heroism, avoiding his power, and wishing to plan for his own preservation.

units.zh: 梁祖經營霸業，外則干戈屢動，內則帑庾俱虛，齊王悉心盡力，傾竭財資助之。）〉
units.en: As the Founder built his empire, wars abroad and empty treasuries at home, the Prince of Qi gave his full support and poured out his wealth to sustain him.)〉
units.literal: The Founder managed his hegemony; externally arms were repeatedly moved, internally treasuries were all empty; the Prince of Qi devoted heart and strength and poured out wealth to assist him.)〉

units.zh: 其年八月，昭宗遇弑，輝王即位。
units.en: That August, Zhaozong was assassinated and Prince Hui took the throne.
units.literal: In the eighth month of that year Zhaozong met assassination; Prince Hui ascended the throne.

units.zh: 十月，復以全義為河南尹，兼忠武軍節度使、判六軍諸衛事。
units.en: In the tenth month Quanyi was restored as Intendant of Henan, with the Zhongwu command and authority over the Six Armies and palace guards.
units.literal: In the tenth month Quanyi was again made Intendant of Henan, concurrently military governor of Zhongwu, and administrator of the Six Armies and all guard offices.

units.zh: 梁祖建號，以全義兼河陽節度使，封魏王。
units.en: When the Liang Founder proclaimed his dynasty, Quanyi received the Heyang command as well and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
units.literal: When the Founder of Liang established his reign title, Quanyi was made concurrent military governor of Heyang and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 開平二年，冊拜太保、兼陝虢節度使、河陽尹。
units.en: In Kaiping 2 he was appointed Grand Guardian, with the Shan-Guo command and the Heyang intendancy.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaiping he was invested as Grand Guardian, concurrent military governor of Shan-Guo, and Intendant of Heyang.

units.zh: 四年，冊拜太傅、河南尹、判六軍，兼鄭、滑等州節度使。
units.en: In year 4 he became Grand Tutor, Intendant of Henan, administrator of the Six Armies, and military governor of Zheng, Hua, and neighboring prefectures.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was invested as Grand Tutor, Intendant of Henan, administrator of the Six Armies, and concurrent military governor of Zheng, Hua, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 乾化元年，冊拜太師。
units.en: In Qianhua 1 he was appointed Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianhua he was invested as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 二年，朱友珪篡逆，以全義為守太尉、河南尹、宋亳節度使兼國計使。
units.en: In year 2, after Zhu Yougui's coup, Quanyi was made Guardian Grand Commandant, Intendant of Henan, governor of Song and Bo, and Commissioner of National Accounts.
units.literal: In the second year Zhu Yougui usurped by treason and made Quanyi Guardian Grand Commandant, Intendant of Henan, military governor of Song and Bo, and concurrent Commissioner of National Accounts.

units.zh: 梁末帝嗣位於汴，以全義為洛京留守，兼鎮河陽。
units.en: When the Last Liang Emperor succeeded at Bian, Quanyi became garrison commander of the Luoyang capital and held Heyang as well.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded at Bian, Quanyi was made Luoyang capital garrison commander and concurrently governed Heyang.

units.zh: 未幾，授天下兵馬副元帥。
units.en: Soon after he was named Deputy Commander-in-Chief of all forces.
units.literal: Before long he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of all armies and horses under Heaven.

units.zh: 末帝季年，趙、張用事，段凝為北面招討使，驟居諸將之右。
units.en: In the Last Emperor's final years Zhao and Zhang dominated court affairs; Duan Ning was made northern campaign commander and suddenly ranked above all other generals.
units.literal: In the Last Emperor's declining years Zhao and Zhang held power; Duan Ning became northern frontier commissioner for suppression and suddenly stood above the other generals.

units.zh: 全義知其不可，遣使啟梁末帝曰：「老臣受先朝重顧，蒙陛下委以副元帥之名。
units.en: Quanyi saw this would not work and sent word to the Last Emperor: "Your servant received great favor from the former court and was honored with the post of Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
units.literal: Quanyi knew this would not do and sent a messenger to report to the Last Emperor of Liang: "This old minister received heavy favor from the former court and was entrusted by Your Majesty with the name of Deputy Commander-in-Chief.

units.zh: 臣雖遲暮，尚可董軍，請付北面兵柄，庶分宵旰。
units.en: Though I am old, I can still command troops; please give me the northern command so I may lighten Your Majesty's burdens.
units.literal: Although your minister is in late years, he can still oversee the army; I beg that the northern military authority be entrusted to me, that I may share Your Majesty's toil night and day.

units.zh: 段凝晚進，德未服人，恐人情不和，敗亂國政。」
units.en: Duan Ning is a newcomer whose virtue has not won men's hearts; I fear discord will disrupt the state."
units.literal: Duan Ning is a late arrival; his virtue has not won men; I fear popular sentiment will not be harmonious and will disrupt and ruin state affairs."

units.zh: 不聽。
units.en: His plea went unheeded.
units.literal: He was not heeded.

units.zh: 全義托朱氏垂三十年，梁祖末年，猜忌宿將，欲害全義者數四，全義單身曲事，悉以家財貢奉。
units.en: Quanyi had served the Zhu clan for nearly thirty years; in the Founder's last years, suspicious of veteran generals, he tried four times to have Quanyi killed; Quanyi humbled himself alone and offered up his entire fortune in tribute.
units.literal: Quanyi relied on the Zhu clan for nearly thirty years; in the Founder's later years he was suspicious of veteran generals and wished to harm Quanyi on four occasions; Quanyi alone bent himself in service and presented all his household wealth in tribute.

units.zh: 洎梁祖河朔喪師之後，月獻鎧馬，以補其軍；
units.en: After the Founder lost his Hebei campaign, Quanyi sent armor and horses every month to replenish the army;
units.literal: After the Founder of Liang lost an army in Hebei, Quanyi presented armor and horses each month to replenish his forces;

units.zh: 又以服勤盡瘁，無以加諸，故竟免於禍。
units.en: and through such tireless devotion there was nothing more to ask of him, and so he escaped harm in the end.
units.literal: and moreover because of his diligent service to exhaustion there was nothing more to add, he ultimately escaped calamity.

units.zh: 全義妻儲氏，明敏有才略。
units.en: Quanyi's wife, Lady Chu, was intelligent and resourceful.
units.literal: Quanyi's wife was Lady Chu; she was bright, keen, and had stratagems.

units.zh: 梁祖自柏鄉失律後，連年親征河朔，心疑全義，或左右讒間，儲氏每入宮，委曲伸理。
units.en: After the disaster at Baxiang the Founder campaigned in Hebei year after year and grew suspicious of Quanyi, with courtiers sometimes slandering him; Lady Chu would visit the palace and patiently set matters straight.
units.literal: After the Founder of Liang lost discipline at Baxiang, for years in succession he personally campaigned in Hebei and Shuo and harbored doubts about Quanyi; sometimes those at his side slandered and alienated; Lady Chu each time entered the palace and tactfully explained the truth.

units.zh: 有時怒不可測，急召全義，儲氏謁見梁祖，厲聲言曰：「宗奭種田叟耳，三十餘年，洛城四面，開荒劚棘，招聚軍賦，資陛下創業。
units.en: When the Founder's anger was unpredictable and he urgently summoned Quanyi, Lady Chu confronted him and said sharply, "Zongyi is nothing but a farmer; for thirty years he cleared the land around Luoyang, gathered supplies, and funded Your Majesty's rise to power.
units.literal: Sometimes his anger was beyond measure; he urgently summoned Quanyi; Lady Chu had an audience with the Founder and said in a stern voice: "Zongyi is just a farming rustic; for more than thirty years on all four sides of Luoyang he opened wasteland and cut thorns, gathered military levies, and supplied Your Majesty's founding enterprise.

units.zh: 今年齒衰朽，指景待盡，而大家疑之，何也？」
units.en: Now he is old and near death—why does Your Majesty still doubt him?"
units.literal: This year his teeth are decayed and worn; he awaits the end by the setting sun—yet the Great One suspects him; why?"

units.zh: 梁祖遽笑而謂曰：「我無惡心，嫗勿多言。」
units.en: The Founder laughed abruptly and said, "I mean him no harm; old woman, say no more."
units.literal: The Founder of Liang hastily laughed and said: "I have no evil intent; old woman, speak no more."

units.zh: 〈（《齊王外傳》云：梁祖猜忌王，慮為後患，前後欲殺之者數四，夫人儲氏麵請梁祖得免，梁祖遂以其子福王納齊王之女。）〉
units.en: (The Unofficial Biography of the Prince of Qi records that the Founder suspected the Prince and tried four times to kill him; Lady Chu pleaded with him in person and saved her husband; the Founder then had his son the Prince of Fu marry the Prince of Qi's daughter.)
units.literal: (《Unofficial Biography of the Prince of Qi》 says: The Founder of Liang was suspicious of the Prince and feared he would be a later trouble; before and after he wished to kill him on four occasions; the lady Chu pleaded face to face with the Founder and he was spared; the Founder then had his son the Prince of Fu marry the Prince of Qi's daughter.)〉

units.zh: 莊宗平梁，全義自洛赴覲，泥首待罪。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Quanyi came from Luoyang to court, prostrating himself to await judgment.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Quanyi came from Luoyang to audience, pressing his face to the ground awaiting punishment.

units.zh: 莊宗撫慰久之，以其年老，令人掖而升殿，宴賜盡歡，詔皇子繼岌、皇弟存紀等皆兄事之。
units.en: The emperor comforted him at length, had attendants help the old man up the hall, feasted him generously, and ordered his son Jiji, his younger brother Cunji, and the others to treat him as an elder brother.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong comforted him for a long time; because he was old, he had men support him to ascend the hall; at the feast gifts were bestowed with full joy; he decreed that the imperial son Jiji, the imperial brother Cunji, and others all treat him as an elder brother.

units.zh: 先是，天祐十五年，梁末帝自汴趨洛，將祀於圓丘。
units.en: Earlier, in Tianyou 15, the Last Liang Emperor had hurried from Bian to Luoyang to perform the Round Mound sacrifice.
units.literal: Earlier, in the fifteenth year of Tianyou, the Last Emperor of Liang hurried from Bian to Luoyang and was about to sacrifice at the Round Mound.

units.zh: 時王師攻下楊劉，徇地曹、濮，梁末帝懼，急歸於汴，其禮不遂，然其法物咸在。
units.en: When the Tang army took Yangliu and advanced into Cao and Pu, the Last Emperor fled back to Bian and the ceremony was never held, but all the ritual implements remained.
units.literal: At that time the royal army captured Yangliu and extended over Cao and Pu; the Last Emperor was afraid and hurried back to Bian; the rite was not completed, but all its ritual implements remained.

units.zh: 至是，全義乃奏曰：「請陛下便幸洛陽，臣已有郊禮之備。」
units.en: Now Quanyi memorialized, "I beg Your Majesty to come to Luoyang at once; I have already prepared everything for the suburban sacrifice."
units.literal: At this time Quanyi memorialized: "I beg Your Majesty to proceed at once to Luoyang; your minister already has the preparations for the suburban rite."

units.zh: 翌日，製以全義復為尚書令、魏王、河南尹。
units.en: The next day he was restored as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Wei, and Intendant of Henan.
units.literal: The next day an edict made Quanyi again Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Wei, and Intendant of Henan.

units.zh: 明年二月，郊禋禮畢，以全義為守太尉中書令、河南尹，改封齊王，兼領河陽。
units.en: The following second month, after the suburban sacrifices were completed, he was made Guardian Grand Commandant and Minister of the Central Secretariat, Intendant of Henan, enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and given Heyang as well.
units.literal: In the second month of the following year, when the suburban and border sacrifices were completed, Quanyi was made Guardian Grand Commandant and Minister of the Central Secretariat, Intendant of Henan, enfeoffment changed to Prince of Qi, and he concurrently held Heyang.

units.zh: 先是，朱梁時供禦所費，皆出河南府，其後孔謙侵削其權，中官各領內司使務，或豪奪其田園居第，全義乃悉錄進納。
units.en: Under the Liang, imperial expenses had all been borne by the Henan prefecture; later Kong Qian stripped his authority, eunuchs took over inner bureau affairs, and some seized his estates by force; Quanyi then registered everything and turned it all over to the court.
units.literal: Earlier, during Zhu Liang the expenses of the imperial supply all came from the Henan prefecture; afterward Kong Qian encroached on and reduced his authority; eunuchs each held inner bureau commissioner affairs; some seized his fields, gardens, and residences by force; Quanyi then recorded all and presented them in submission.

units.zh: 四年，落河南尹，授忠武軍節度使、檢校太師、尚書令。
units.en: In year 4 he relinquished the Henan intendancy and was given the Zhongwu command as Acting Grand Preceptor and Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was removed as Intendant of Henan and given the military governorship of Zhongwu, Acting Grand Preceptor, and Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 會趙在禮據魏州，都軍進討無功。
units.en: When Zhao Zaili seized Weizhou, the imperial army's campaign against him failed.
units.literal: When Zhao Zaili held Weizhou, the commander's army advanced to attack without success.

units.zh: 時明宗已為群小間諜，端居私第。
units.en: By then Emperor Mingzong had been isolated by petty men and was living quietly at home.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Mingzong had already been alienated and spied upon by petty men and dwelt quietly in his private residence.

units.zh: 全義以臥疾聞變，憂懼不食，薨於洛陽私第，時年七十五。
units.en: Bedridden, Quanyi heard of the upheaval, grew so anxious he would not eat, and died at his home in Luoyang at the age of seventy-five.
units.literal: Quanyi, lying ill, heard of the change, was anxious and fearful and would not eat; he died at his private residence in Luoyang at the age of seventy-five.

units.zh: 天成初，冊贈太師，諡曰忠肅。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was posthumously invested as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

units.zh: 全義曆守太師、太傅、太尉、中書令，封王，邑萬三千戶。
units.en: Over his career Quanyi served as Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Minister of the Central Secretariat, was created a prince, and received a fief of thirteen thousand households.
units.literal: Quanyi in succession held the posts of Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant, and Minister of the Central Secretariat, was enfeoffed as a prince, and his fief was thirteen thousand households.

units.zh: 凡領方鎮洛、鄆、陝、滑、宋，三蒞河陽，再領許州，內外官曆二十九任，尹正河、洛，凡四十年，位極人臣，善保終吉者，蓋一人而已。
units.en: He governed the circuits of Luoyang, Yanzhou, Shanzhou, Huazhou, and Songzhou; thrice held Heyang and twice Xuzhou; filled twenty-nine posts at court and in the provinces; for forty years directed the Yellow River and Luo regions; rose to the summit of power—and of those who kept fortune and a peaceful death, he may have stood alone.
units.literal: In all he governed the regional commands of Luo, Yan, Shan, Hua, and Song; thrice came to Heyang; twice held Xuzhou; held twenty-nine offices inside and outside; was chief magistrate of the Yellow River and Luo regions for forty years; reached the apex of subjects; for securing a good end in safety, perhaps he alone.

units.zh: 全義樸厚大度，敦本務實，起戰士而忘功名，尊儒業而樂善道。
units.en: Plain, generous, and grounded in practical work, he had risen from the ranks yet cared little for glory, honored scholarship, and took pleasure in doing good.
units.literal: Quanyi was plain, thick, and magnanimous, devoted to fundamentals and practical affairs, rose from a fighting man yet forgot fame and merit, honored Confucian learning and delighted in the good Way.

units.zh: 家非士族，而獎愛衣冠，開幕府辟士，必求望實，屬邑補奏，不任吏人。
units.en: Though no aristocrat by birth, he favored men of learning, opened his staff only to those of real standing, and when filling county posts submitted his own nominees rather than leave the choice to routine bureaucrats.
units.literal: His family was not of the scholar-official clans, yet he encouraged and loved the gentry; when opening a staff office and recruiting scholars he always sought reputation and substance; for subordinate counties he submitted recommendations for appointment and did not employ clerks and petty officials.

units.zh: 位極王公，不衣羅綺，心奉釋、老，而不溺左道。
units.en: At the height of princely rank he still shunned silks, honored Buddhism and Daoism in private, yet never fell into occult excess.
units.literal: His rank reached prince and duke, yet he did not wear gauze and brocade; in heart he served Buddhism and Daoism, yet did not drown in heterodox ways.

units.zh: 如是數者，人以為難。
units.en: In such matters people thought him hard to match.
units.literal: Such several matters—people regarded them as difficult.

units.zh: 自莊宗至洛陽，趨向者皆由徑以希恩寵，全義不改素履，盡誠而已。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong reached Luoyang, courtiers scrambled for favor by every shortcut; Quanyi kept his old ways and offered only straightforward loyalty.
units.literal: From the time Emperor Zhuangzong came to Luoyang, those who rushed to court all took shortcuts hoping for favor and grace; Quanyi did not alter his plain conduct and gave full sincerity only.

units.zh: 言事者以梁祖為我世讎，宜斫棺燔柩，全義獨上章申理，議者嘉之。
units.en: Memorialists urged that the Liang Founder's body be disinterred and burned as the dynasty's ancient enemy; Quanyi alone memorialized in defense of proper treatment, and critics applauded him.
units.literal: Those who spoke on affairs held that the Founder of Liang was our hereditary foe and that his coffin should be hacked open and his bier burned; Quanyi alone submitted a memorial to set forth reason; discussers praised this.

units.zh: 劉皇后嘗從莊宗幸其第，奏云：「妾孩幼遇亂，失父母，欲拜全義為義父。」
units.en: Empress Liu once accompanied Zhuangzong to his house and said, "In childhood I was orphaned by the wars and wish to take Quanyi as my adoptive father."
units.literal: Empress Liu once followed Emperor Zhuangzong in visiting his residence and memorialized, saying: "Your servant as a child met disorder, lost father and mother, and wishes to bow to Quanyi as adoptive father."

units.zh: 許之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: Permission was granted.

units.zh: 全義稽首奏曰：「皇后萬國之母儀，古今未有此事，臣無地自處。」
units.en: Quanyi kowtowed and protested, "The Empress is mother to the realm; such a thing is unheard of in history, and I have no place to put myself."
units.literal: Quanyi kowtowed and memorialized, saying: "The Empress is the mother model of ten thousand states; from ancient to present there has never been such a matter; your servant has no ground on which to place himself."

units.zh: 莊宗敦逼再三，不獲已，乃受劉後之拜。
units.en: Zhuangzong pressed him repeatedly until he could not refuse and accepted the Empress's bow.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong pressed him earnestly again and again; unable to refuse, he then received Empress Liu's bow.

units.zh: 既非所願，君子不以為非。
units.en: Because he had not wanted it, fair-minded readers do not hold it against him.
units.literal: Since it was not his wish, gentlemen do not regard it as wrong.

units.zh: 然全義少長軍中，立性樸滯，凡百姓有詞訟，以先訴者為得理，以是人多枉濫，為時所非。
units.en: Yet he had grown up in the army and was slow by nature: in lawsuits whoever came first was deemed right, so many suffered injustice and contemporaries faulted him for it.
units.literal: Yet Quanyi from youth grew up in the army and by nature was plain and dull; whenever common people had lawsuits, whoever sued first was held to have reason—thus many were wronged and excessive, and he was disapproved by the age.

units.zh: 又嘗怒河南縣令羅貫，因憑劉後譖於莊宗，俾貫非罪而死，露屍於府門，冤枉之聲，聞於遠近，斯亦良玉之微瑕也。
units.en: He also took offense at Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, and through Empress Liu's slander had him executed without cause and his body left at the prefecture gate; the cry of injustice spread far and wide—a small stain on an otherwise fine reputation.
units.literal: He also once grew angry at Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, and by relying on Empress Liu slandered him to Emperor Zhuangzong, causing Guan to die without crime; his corpse was exposed at the prefectural gate; the sound of wrongful suffering was heard far and near—this too is a slight flaw in fine jade.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：梁乾化元年七月辛丑，梁祖幸全義私第。
units.en: (Supplemental Texts of the Five Dynasties: On the xinchou day of the seventh month of Liang's first Qianhua year, the Liang Founder visited Quanyi at his private residence.
units.literal: (Supplemental Texts of the Five Dynasties: In the seventh month of the first year of Qianhua of Liang, on the day xinchou, the Founder of Liang visited Quanyi's private residence.

units.zh: 甲辰，歸大內。
units.en: On jiachen he returned to the palace.
units.literal: On the day jiachen he returned to the great inner palace.

units.zh: 梁史稱：「上不豫，厭秋暑，幸宗奭私第數日，宰臣視事於仁政亭，崇政諸司並止於河南府廨署。」
units.en: The Liang History says, "The emperor was unwell and, weary of the autumn heat, stayed several days at Zongyi's home while the chief ministers handled affairs at the Hall of Benevolent Government and Chongzheng offices were lodged at the Henan prefecture."
units.literal: The Liang History states: "The Emperor was unwell, weary of autumn heat, and visited Zongyi's private residence for several days; the chief ministers conducted affairs at the Hall of Benevolent Government; all offices of Chongzheng likewise halted at the Henan prefectural yamen."

units.zh: 世傳梁祖亂全義之家，婦女悉皆進禦，其子繼祚不勝憤恥，欲事刂刃於梁祖。
units.en: Tradition holds that the Liang Founder ravaged Quanyi's household, that all the women were taken for the palace, and that his son Jizuo, shamed beyond bearing, meant to strike the Founder down.
units.literal: The age transmits that the Founder of Liang violated Quanyi's household, and all the women were presented to the imperial bed; his son Jizuo could not bear rage and shame and wished to draw a blade against the Founder of Liang.

units.zh: 全義止之曰：「吾頃在河陽，遭李罕之之難，引太原軍圍閉經年，啖木屑以度朝夕，死在頃刻，得他救援，以至今日，此恩不可負也。」
units.en: Quanyi stopped him, saying, "When I was at Heyang, Li Hanzhi brought the Taiyuan army to besiege me for a full year. I survived from day to day on wood shavings and expected death at any moment, until another came to my rescue and brought me to where I am today. I cannot betray that kindness."
units.literal: Quanyi stopped him, saying: "I lately was at Heyang and met Li Hanzhi's calamity; he brought the Taiyuan army to besiege and close for a full year; I ate wood shavings to pass mornings and evenings; death was in the next moment; I received another's rescue to reach today—this grace cannot be betrayed."

units.zh: 其子乃止。
units.en: His son desisted.
units.literal: His son then stopped.

units.zh: 梁史云云者，諱國惡也。
units.en: The Liang History's bland account is a cover for national disgrace.
units.literal: The Liang History's such-and-such words are concealing the state's evil.

units.zh: 臣謹案，《春秋》莊二年，《經》曰：「十有二月，夫人薑氏會齊侯於禚。」
units.en: I note that the Spring and Autumn Annals for Duke Zhuang's second year records in the Classic, "In the twelfth month the Lady Jiang met the Marquis of Qi at Zhen."
units.literal: Your servant respectfully examines: in the second year of Duke Zhuang in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Classic says: "In the twelfth month the Lady Jiang met the Marquis of Qi at Zhen."

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「書奸也。」
units.en: The Commentary explains, "This records adultery."
units.literal: The Commentary says: "It records adultery."

units.zh: 夫《經》言會者，諱惡，禮也；
units.en: When the Classic says "met," it euphemizes the crime—that is ritual propriety;
units.literal: Now when the Classic says "met," it conceals evil—this is ritual propriety;

units.zh: 《傳》書奸者，暴其罪以垂誡也。
units.en: when the Commentary writes "adultery," it exposes the sin as a warning to posterity.
units.literal: when the Commentary writes "adultery," it exposes the crime to hand down warning.

units.zh: 又《莊》二十二年，《傳》書：陳完飲桓公酒，公曰：「以火繼之。」
units.en: Again, in Duke Zhuang's twenty-second year the Commentary tells how Chen Wan drank with Duke Huan, who said, "Let the lamps follow."
units.literal: Again, in the twenty-second year of Duke Zhuang, the Commentary records: Chen Wan drank with Duke Huan of Qi; the Duke said: "Continue with fire."

units.zh: 辭曰：「臣卜其晝，未卜其夜。」
units.en: Chen declined, "I divined for the day, not for the night."
units.literal: He declined, saying: "Your servant divined for the day, not for the night."

units.zh: 豈有天子幸人臣之家，留止數日，奸亂萌矣。
units.en: Can a Son of Heaven lodge for days in a subject's house without scandal taking root?
units.literal: How could there be a Son of Heaven visiting a subject's house and staying several days without the sprouting of adultery and disorder?

units.zh: 況全義本出巢賊，敗依河陽節度使諸葛爽，爽用為澤州刺史，及爽死，全義事爽子仲方，即與李罕之同逐仲方，罕之帥河陽，全義為河南尹，未幾，又逐罕之，自據河陽，其翻覆也如此。
units.en: Moreover Quanyi had begun among Huang Chao's rebels, then attached himself to Zhuge Shuang of Heyang, who made him prefect of Zezhou; after Shuang's death he served Shuang's son Zhongfang, then with Li Hanzhi expelled Zhongfang; when Hanzhi held Heyang, Quanyi became Intendant of Henan, and soon expelled Hanzhi to seize Heyang himself—so fickle was his course.
units.literal: Moreover Quanyi originally came forth from Huang Chao's bandits; defeated, he relied on the Heyang military governor Zhuge Shuang; Shuang employed him as prefect of Zezhou; when Shuang died, Quanyi served Shuang's son Zhongfang, then together with Li Hanzhi drove out Zhongfang; Hanzhi commanded Heyang, Quanyi was Intendant of Henan; before long he again drove out Hanzhi and himself held Heyang—his turning and overturning were thus.

units.zh: 自是托跡朱梁，斫喪唐室，惟勤勸課，其實斂民附賊，以固恩寵。
units.en: Thereafter he cast his lot with the Zhu Liang, helped ruin the Tang, and though he preached diligence in farming, in truth he taxed the people dry and clung to the usurpers for favor.
units.literal: From this he entrusted his footsteps to Zhu Liang, hacked away and ruined the Tang house; only diligently urged tax collection—in truth he squeezed the people and attached to the rebel to secure favor and grace.

units.zh: 梁時，月進鎧馬，以補軍實。
units.en: Under the Liang he sent armored horses every month to fill the army's needs.
units.literal: In Liang times, each month he presented armored horses to supplement military stores.

units.zh: 及梁祖為友珪所弑，首進錢一百萬，以助山陵。
units.en: When the Liang Founder was murdered by Zhu Yougui, he was the first to offer a million cash toward the imperial burial.
units.literal: When the Founder of Liang was murdered by Yougui, he was first to present one million in cash to assist the imperial tomb.

units.zh: 莊宗平中原，全義合與敬翔、李振等族誅，又通賂於劉皇后，乘莊宗幸洛，言臣已有郊天費用。
units.en: When Zhuangzong conquered the Central Plain, Quanyi deserved execution with Jing Xiang, Li Zhen, and their kin; he bribed Empress Liu and, when Zhuangzong came to Luoyang, claimed he already had funds for the suburban sacrifice.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the Central Plain, Quanyi ought to have been exterminated with Jing Xiang, Li Zhen, and their clans; again he bribed Empress Liu; seizing when Zhuangzong visited Luoyang, he said your servant already has the expenses for suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

units.zh: 夫全義匹夫也，豈能自殖財賦，其剝下奉上也又如此。
units.en: A commoner like Quanyi could not have amassed such wealth on his own; he extorted the people to court the throne just as before.
units.literal: Now Quanyi was a common fellow—how could he by himself increase wealth and taxes? His stripping those below to serve those above was again thus.

units.zh: 晚年保證明宗，欲為子孫之福，師方渡河，鄴都兵亂，全義憂憾不食，終以餓死。
units.en: In old age he backed Mingzong, hoping to secure his line; when the Yedu mutiny broke out as the army crossed the river, he grieved himself into refusing food and starved to death.
units.literal: In his late years he guaranteed and protected Emperor Mingzong, wishing fortune for sons and grandsons; the army was just crossing the river when the troops at Yedu mutinied; Quanyi, anxious and resentful, would not eat and in the end died of starvation.

units.zh: 未死前，其子繼業訟弟汝州防禦使繼孫，莊宗貶房州司戶，賜自盡。
units.en: Before he died his son Jiye denounced his brother Jisun, defender of Ruzhou; Zhuangzong reduced Jisun to registrar at Fangzhou and ordered him to take his own life.
units.literal: Before his death his son Jiye sued his younger brother, Defender of Ruzhou Jisun; Emperor Zhuangzong demoted him to registrar of Fangzhou and granted self-extermination.

units.zh: 其制略曰：「侵奪父權，惑亂家事，繼鳥獸之行，畜梟獍之心。」
units.en: The edict in brief read, "He usurped his father's authority, threw the household into disorder, followed the ways of beasts, and harbored a treacherous heart."
units.literal: The outline of the edict said: "He encroached on and seized the father's authority, confused and disordered household affairs, continued the conduct of birds and beasts, and nourished the heart of an owl and a jackal."

units.zh: 其禦家無法也又如此。
units.en: So little command did he have over his own house.
units.literal: His governing the family without law was again thus.

units.zh: 河南令羅貫，方正文章之士，事全義稍慢，全義怒告劉皇后，斃貫於枯木之下，朝野冤之。
units.en: Luo Guan of Henan, a principled scholar-official, showed Quanyi slight disrespect; Quanyi complained to Empress Liu and had him killed under a dead tree, to the outrage of court and country.
units.literal: Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan, was an upright man of letters; in serving Quanyi he was slightly slow; Quanyi in anger reported to Empress Liu and had Guan executed beneath a withered tree; court and countryside deemed it wrongful.

units.zh: 洛陽監軍使嘗收得李太尉平泉莊醒酒石，全義求之，監軍不與，全義立殺之，其附勢作威也又如此。
units.en: When the Luoyang army supervisor acquired the sobering stone from Chancellor Li Deyu's Pingquan estate, Quanyi demanded it; refused, he had the man killed on the spot—another instance of bullying by power.
units.literal: The Luoyang army supervisor once obtained the sobering stone from Grand Commandant Li's Pingquan estate; Quanyi sought it; the supervisor would not give it; Quanyi immediately killed him—his clinging to power and making might were again thus.

units.zh: 蓋亂世賊臣耳，得保首領，為幸已多。
units.en: He was nothing but a rebel minister of chaotic times; keeping his head was luck enough.
units.literal: In sum he was a rebel minister of a chaotic age; to preserve his head was already much fortune.

units.zh: 晉天福中，其子繼祚謀反伏誅，識者知餘殃在其子孫也。
units.en: In Later Jin's Tianfu era his son Jizuo rebelled and was executed, and observers knew the family's punishment was not yet spent.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin his son Jizuo plotted rebellion and was executed; those who knew saw that remaining calamity lay on his sons and grandsons.

units.zh: 臣讀《莊宗實錄》，見史官敘《全義傳》，虛美尤甚，至今負俗無識之士，尚以全義為名臣，故因補闕文，粗論事跡雲。）〉
units.en: Reading Zhuangzong's Veritable Records, I find the historians' account of Quanyi extravagantly flattering; vulgar men even now call him a great minister—hence this supplement, a rough review of his career.)〉
units.literal: Your servant read the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhuangzong and saw the historiographers narrate the "Biography of Quanyi" with empty praise especially severe; down to today vulgar men without understanding still take Quanyi as a famous minister—therefore, by supplementing the missing text, I roughly discuss his deeds, thus.)〉

units.zh: 朱友謙，字德光，許州人，本名簡。
units.en: Zhu Youqian, courtesy name Deguang, came from Xuzhou; he was originally named Jian.
units.literal: Zhu Youqian, styled Deguang, was a man of Xuzhou; his original name was Jian.

units.zh: 祖岩，父琮，世為陳、許小校。
units.en: His grandfather Yan and his father Cong had for generations served as minor officers in Chen and Xu.
units.literal: His grandfather was Yan, his father Cong; for generations they were petty officers of Chen and Xu.

units.zh: 廣明之亂，簡去鄉里，事澠池鎮將柏夔為部隸。
units.en: During the Guangming upheaval he left home and joined the Mianchi garrison commander Bai Kui as a company man.
units.literal: In the disorder of Guangming, Jian left his home district and served the Mianchi garrison commander Bai Kui as a company subordinate.

units.zh: 嘗為盜於石壕、三鄉之間，剽劫行旅。
units.en: He had once robbed travelers between Shihao and Sanxiang.
units.literal: He once was a bandit between Shihao and Sanxiang, plundering and robbing travelers.

units.zh: 後事陝州節度使王珙，積勞至軍校。
units.en: He later entered the service of Wang Gong, military governor of Shanzhou, and rose by merit to regimental commander.
units.literal: Later he served the Shanzhou military governor Wang Gong and through accumulated merit reached army commander.

units.zh: 珙性嚴急，禦下無恩，牙將李璠者，珙深所倚愛，小有違忤，暴加箠擊，璠陰銜之。
units.en: Wang Gong was harsh and graceless toward his men; Li Fan, a favored staff officer, bore the brunt of his rage at the slightest offense and secretly nursed a grudge.
units.literal: Wang Gong was harsh and graceless toward his men; Li Fan, a favored staff officer, bore the brunt of his rage at the slightest offense and secretly nursed a grudge.

units.zh: 光化元年，珙與弟河中節度使珂相持，干戈日尋，珙兵屢敗，部伍離心。
units.en: In 898 Wang Gong and his brother Ke, military governor of Hezhong, fell into open war; Gong's armies kept losing and his troops lost heart.
units.literal: In the first year of Guanghua, Gong and his younger brother the Hezhong military governor Ke confronted each other; arms were sought day by day; Gong's troops repeatedly were defeated; the ranks lost heart.

units.zh: 二年六月，璠殺珙，歸附汴人，梁祖表璠為陝州節度使。
units.en: In the sixth month of the following year Fan killed Gong, went over to the Liang, and the Liang Founder had him appointed military governor of Shanzhou.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the second year Fan killed Gong, submitted to the Bian men, and the Founder of Liang memorialized Fan as military governor of Shanzhou.

units.zh: 璠亦苛慘，軍情不葉，簡復攻璠，璠冒刃獲免，逃歸於汴。
units.en: Fan proved cruel as well and lost the army's loyalty; Jian attacked him again; Fan barely escaped the blades and fled to Bian.
units.literal: Fan also was harsh and cruel; army sentiment was not harmonious; Jian again attacked Fan; Fan braved blades and escaped, fled and returned to Bian.

units.zh: 三年，梁祖表簡為陝州留後。
units.en: In the third year the Liang Founder appointed Jian acting governor of Shanzhou.
units.literal: In the third year the Founder of Liang memorialized Jian as acting governor of Shanzhou.

units.zh: 九月，天子授以旄鉞。
units.en: In the ninth month the emperor formally invested him with the command.
units.literal: In the ninth month the Son of Heaven invested him with banner and axe.

units.zh: 車駕在鳳翔，梁祖往來，簡事之益謹，奏授平章事。
units.en: While the court was at Fengxiang and the Liang Founder shuttled back and forth, Jian served him with growing devotion and was recommended for Grand Councilor.
units.literal: The imperial carriage was at Fengxiang; the Founder of Liang came and went; Jian served him with increasing care and was memorialized to receive Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 天復末，昭宗遷都洛陽，駐蹕於陝。
units.en: Late in Tianfu, Emperor Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang and paused at Shanzhou.
units.literal: At the end of Tianfu, Emperor Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang and halted the imperial progress at Shan.

units.zh: 時朝士經亂，簪裳不備，簡獻上百副，請給百官，朝容稍備。
units.en: Courtiers still lacked proper dress after the wars; Jian presented a hundred sets of regalia for the officials, and the court's appearance was partly restored.
units.literal: At that time court gentlemen had passed through disorder; caps and robes were not complete; Jian presented a hundred sets and requested they be given to the hundred officials; court appearance was slightly made ready.

units.zh: 以迎奉功，遷檢校侍中。
units.en: For escorting the emperor he was promoted to Acting Palace Attendant.
units.literal: For the merit of welcoming and attending, he was transferred to Acting Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 簡與梁祖同宗，乃陳情於梁祖曰：「仆位崇將相，比無勳勞，皆元帥令公生成之造也。
units.en: Sharing the Zhu clan, Jian appealed to the Founder, saying, "I stand among the highest ministers yet have earned no merit; all I am I owe to Your Excellency's grace.
units.literal: Jian was of the same clan as the Founder of Liang; he then laid forth his feelings to the Founder, saying: "Your servant's rank is lofty as general and minister, yet compared with others has no merit or toil—all is the Marshal Commander's life-giving creation.

units.zh: 願以微生灰粉為效，乞以姓名，肩隨宗室。」
units.en: I would lay down my life in your service and beg to take a name and rank beside your house."
units.literal: I wish to take my slight life as ash and powder for effect, and beg that with my surname and personal name I may shoulder and follow the imperial clan."

units.zh: 梁祖深賞其心，乃名之為友謙，編入屬籍，待遇同於己子。
units.en: The Founder was deeply moved, renamed him Youqian, enrolled him in the imperial clan, and treated him like his own son.
units.literal: The Founder of Liang deeply appreciated his heart, then named him Youqian, entered him in the clan register, and treated him the same as his own sons.

units.zh: 友謙亦盡心葉讚，功烈居多。
units.en: Youqian in turn served him wholeheartedly and won many victories.
units.literal: Youqian also gave full heart in supporting and praising; achievements and exploits were especially many.

units.zh: 梁祖建號，移授河中節度使、檢校太尉，累拜中書令，封冀王。
units.en: When the Liang Founder took the throne, he was made military governor of Hezhong and Acting Grand Commandant, later Minister of the Central Secretariat and Prince of Ji.
units.literal: When the Founder of Liang established his reign title, he was transferred and given the Hezhong military governorship and Acting Grand Commandant, repeatedly invested as Minister of the Central Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.

units.zh: 及朱友珪弑逆，友謙意不懌，雖勉奉偽命，中懷怏怏。
units.en: When Zhu Yougui murdered his father, Youqian was displeased; though he outwardly obeyed the usurper, inwardly he seethed.
units.literal: When Zhu Yougui committed regicide, Youqian's mind was not pleased; although he strained to follow the false command, within he harbored resentment.

units.zh: 友珪征之，友謙辭以北面侵軼，謂賓友曰：「友珪是先帝假子，敢行大逆，餘位列維城，恩逾父子，論功校德，何讓伊人，詎以平生附托之恩，屈身於逆豎之手！」
units.en: When Yougui marched against him, Youqian pleaded northern incursions and told his staff, "Yougui is only the late emperor's adopted son yet dares regicide; I rank among the empire's bulwarks and have been honored beyond father and son—in merit and virtue I yield to no one. Shall lifelong trust make me bow to a usurper?"
units.literal: Yougui campaigned against him; Youqian declined on the grounds of northern frontier raids and said to guests and friends: "Yougui is the late Emperor's adopted son yet dares to commit great treason; I by rank stand among the walls of the state, grace exceeding father and son; weighing merit and comparing virtue, how would I yield to that man? How could I, for the grace of lifelong trust, bend my body to the hands of a rebellious villain!"

units.zh: 遂不奉命。
units.en: He refused the order.
units.literal: He then did not obey the command.

units.zh: 其年八月，友珪遣大將牛存節、康懷英、韓攻之，友謙乞師於莊宗。
units.en: That eighth month Yougui sent Niu Cunjie, Kang Huaiying, and Han against him; Youqian appealed to Zhuangzong for aid.
units.literal: In the eighth month of that year Yougui sent the great generals Niu Cunjie, Kang Huaiying, and Han to attack him; Youqian begged troops from Emperor Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗親總軍赴援，與汴軍遇於平陽，大破之。
units.en: Zhuangzong led the army in person, met the Bian forces at Pingyang, and routed them.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong personally led the army to rush to aid; he met the Bian army at Pingyang and greatly defeated it.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：晉王出澤潞以救之，追懷英於解縣，大敗之。
units.en: (Ouyang Xiu's History: The Prince of Jin marched through Ze and Lu to relieve him, pursued Kang Huaiying to Jie County, and crushed him.
units.literal: (Ouyang Xiu's History: The Prince of Jin marched out through Ze and Lu to rescue him, pursued Huaiying at Jie County, and greatly defeated him.

units.zh: 追至白逕嶺，夜秉炬擊之，懷英又敗。）〉
units.en: He pursued to Baijing Ridge and attacked by torchlight at night; Huaiying was beaten again.)〉
units.literal: Pursuing to Baijing Ridge, at night bearing torches he struck them; Huaiying was again defeated.)〉

units.zh: 因與友謙會於猗氏，友謙盛陳感慨，願敦盟約，莊宗歡甚。
units.en: He then met Youqian at Yishi; Youqian poured out his feelings and asked for a firm alliance, and Zhuangzong was delighted.
units.literal: Thereupon he met Youqian at Yishi; Youqian fully set forth emotion and wished to deepen the covenant; Emperor Zhuangzong was very pleased.

units.zh: 友謙乘醉鼾寢於帳中，莊宗熟視之，謂左右曰：「冀王真貴人也，但恨其臂短耳。」
units.en: Youqian fell asleep snoring in his tent; Zhuangzong studied him and said to his attendants, "The Prince of Ji is a man of true nobility—only pity his arms are short."
units.literal: Youqian, riding drunkenness, snored asleep in the tent; Emperor Zhuangzong gazed at him intently and said to those at hand: "The Prince of Ji is truly a noble man, only I regret his arms are short."

units.zh: 及梁末帝嗣位，以恩禮結其心；
units.en: When the Last Liang Emperor succeeded, he won him back with courtesy;
units.literal: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded, he bound his heart with grace and ritual;

units.zh: 友謙亦遜辭稱藩，行其正朔。
units.en: Youqian in turn submitted as a vassal and observed the Liang calendar.
units.literal: Youqian also with yielding words called himself a vassal and followed their reign calendar.

units.zh: 天祐十七年，友謙襲取同州，以其子令德為帥，請節鉞於梁，不獲。
units.en: In 920 Youqian seized Tongzhou, installed his son Lingde as commander, and asked the Liang for formal investiture but was refused.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianyou, Youqian surprised and took Tongzhou, made his son Lingde commander, and requested the command banner and axe from Liang but did not obtain it.

units.zh: 友謙即請之於莊宗，令幕客王正言以節旄賜之，梁將劉鄩、尹皓攻同州，友謙來告急，莊宗遣李嗣昭、李存審將兵赴之，敗汴軍於滑北，解圍而還。
units.en: He then asked Zhuangzong, who had his aide Wang Zhengyan grant the commission; when Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao besieged Tongzhou, Youqian appealed for help; Zhuangzong sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen, who defeated the Bian army north of Huazhou and lifted the siege.
units.literal: Youqian then requested it from Emperor Zhuangzong and had his staff member Wang Zhengyan bestow the command regalia; Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao attacked Tongzhou; Youqian came to report urgency; Zhuangzong sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen to lead troops thither, defeated the Bian army north of Hua, lifted the siege, and returned.

units.zh: 初，劉鄩兵至蒲中，倉儲匱乏，人心離貳，軍民將校，鹹欲歸梁。
units.en: When Liu Yan first reached central Pu, stores ran low, morale split, and soldiers and civilians alike wanted to go over to the Liang.
units.literal: At first when Liu Yan's troops reached the center of Pu, granaries and stores were exhausted, men's hearts were divided in two, and army and people, commanders and officers—all wished to return to Liang.

units.zh: 友謙諸子令錫等亦說其父曰：「晉王雖推心於我，然懸兵赴援，急維相應，寧我負人，擇福宜重。
units.en: Youqian's sons, including Lingxi, also urged him, "The Prince of Jin may trust us, but his army is far away and the crisis is near—better to wrong a friend than miss our chance; choose the stronger side.
units.literal: Youqian's sons Lingxi and others also urged their father, saying: "Although the Prince of Jin opens his heart to us, yet with distant troops rushing to aid, urgent ties must correspond—better that I wrong others; in choosing fortune one should weigh heavily.

units.zh: 請納款於梁，候劉鄩兵退後，與晉王修好。」
units.en: Submit to the Liang now, and after Liu Yan withdraws restore friendship with Jin."
units.literal: Please submit allegiance to Liang; wait until Liu Yan's troops withdraw, then renew good relations with the Prince of Jin."

units.zh: 友謙曰：「晉王親赴予急，夜半秉燭戰賊，麵為盟誓，不負初心。
units.en: Youqian replied, "The Prince of Jin came in person to my aid, fought the enemy by candlelight at midnight, and swore face to face—I will not betray that bond.
units.literal: Youqian said: "The Prince of Jin personally came to my aid, fought the enemy by torchlight at midnight, made a covenant with me face to face, and has not betrayed his original commitment.

units.zh: 昨聞吾告難，命將星行，助我資糧，分我衣屨，而欲翻覆背惠，所謂鄧祁侯云『人將不食吾餘』也。」
units.en: When I called for help he sent his generals at once, supplied my army, and shared his own clothing—yet you would turn traitor to such kindness? That is the warning of Duke Qi of Deng: men will refuse the leavings of one who breaks faith."
units.literal: Only recently, upon hearing my appeal for aid, he ordered his generals to march by starlight, supplied me with provisions, and shared his clothing and footwear with me; yet you would reverse course and betray his kindness. This is what Duke Qi of Deng meant when he said, 'Men will not eat what I leave behind.'"

units.zh: 及破梁軍，加守太尉、西平王。
units.en: After the Liang army was defeated, he was made Guardian Grand Commandant and Prince of Xiping.
units.literal: When the Liang army was broken, he was added Guardian Grand Commandant and Prince of Xiping.

units.zh: 同光元年，莊宗滅梁，友謙覲於洛陽。
units.en: In 923, when Zhuangzong destroyed the Liang, Youqian had an audience in Luoyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Tongguang, Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang; Youqian had an audience at Luoyang.

units.zh: 莊宗置宴饗勞，寵錫無算，親酌觴屬友謙曰：「成吾大業者，公之力也。」
units.en: Zhuangzong feasted and rewarded him beyond measure, poured his own cup, and said, "My great enterprise was your doing."
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong held a banquet to entertain and reward him, bestowing favors and gifts beyond reckoning; he personally poured a cup and offered it to Youqian, saying: "It was through your strength, sir, that I accomplished my great enterprise."

units.zh: 既歸藩，請割慈、隰二郡，依舊隸河中，不許，詔以絳州隸之。
units.en: Back in his domain he asked that Ci and Xi be restored to Hezhong; the court refused but attached Jiangzhou to his command.
units.literal: After returning to his fief, he requested to cut off the two prefectures Ci and Xi and have them again subordinate to Hezhong; it was not permitted; an edict made Jiangzhou subordinate to him.

units.zh: 又請解縣兩池榷鹽，每額輸省課，許之。
units.en: He also won the right to tax the two salt pools at Jie County, paying a fixed levy to the court.
units.literal: He again requested the two salt monopoly pools of Jie County; each quota would pay provincial tax; this was granted.

units.zh: 及郊禮畢，以友謙為守太師、尚書令，進食邑至萬八千戶。
units.en: After the suburban sacrifices he was made Guardian Grand Preceptor and Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, with a fief increased to eighteen thousand households.
units.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, Youqian was made Guardian Grand Preceptor and Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, and his fief advanced to eighteen thousand households.

units.zh: 三年，賜姓，名繼麟，編入屬籍，賜之鐵券，恕死罪。
units.en: In the third year he received the imperial surname, was renamed Jilin, enrolled in the clan register, and granted an iron certificate exempting him from capital punishment.
units.literal: In the third year he was granted the imperial surname, named Jilin, entered in the clan register, and was granted an iron covenant forgiving the death penalty.

units.zh: 以其子令德為遂州節度使，令錫為許州節度使。
units.en: His sons Lingde and Lingxi were made military governors of Suizhou and Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: His son Lingde was made military governor of Suizhou, Lingxi military governor of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 一門三鎮，諸子為刺史者六七人，將校剖竹者又五六人，恩寵之盛，時無與比。
units.en: Three circuits in one family, six or seven sons as prefects, and five or six officers as prefects besides—no favor of the age matched his.
units.literal: One family held three commands; sons as prefects numbered six or seven; commanders and officers receiving carved bamboo tallies were again five or six—the fullness of favor and grace, the age had none to compare.

units.zh: 莊宗季年，稍怠庶政，巷伯伶官，干預國事。
units.en: In Zhuangzong's last years he neglected government; eunuchs and actor-favorites meddled in state affairs.
units.literal: In Emperor Zhuangzong's late years he slightly slackened in common governance; lane eunuchs and actor-officials interfered in state affairs.

units.zh: 時方面諸侯皆行賂遺，或求賂於繼麟，雖僶俛應奉，不滿其請。
units.en: Regional lords all sent bribes; some demanded them from Jilin, and though he strained to comply, he could not meet their demands.
units.literal: At that time regional lords all practiced bribery and gifts; some sought bribes from Jilin; although he bent low in compliance, he did not satisfy their requests.

units.zh: 且曰：「河中土薄民貧，厚貺難辦。」
units.en: He added, "Hezhong's soil is thin and the people poor—lavish gifts are hard to provide."
units.literal: Moreover he said: "Hezhong's soil is thin and the people poor; heavy gifts are hard to provide."

units.zh: 由是群小鹹怨，遂加誣構。
units.en: The court parasites resented him and began to fabricate charges.
units.literal: Thereupon the petty men all resented him and then added slander and fabrication.

units.zh: 郭崇韜討巴、蜀，征師於河中，繼麟令其子令德率師赴之。
units.en: When Guo Chongtao campaigned in Ba and Shu he called on Hezhong for troops, and Jilin sent his son Lingde at the head of the army.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao campaigned against Ba and Shu and requisitioned troops from Hezhong; Jilin ordered his son Lingde to lead the army to go thither.

units.zh: 伶官景進與其黨構曰：「昨王師初起，繼麟以為討己，頗有拒命之意，若不除移，如國家有急，必為後患。」
units.en: The actor Jing Jin and his clique plotted, saying, "When the imperial army first marched, Jilin thought it was aimed at him and nearly refused the order; unless he is removed, he will be a danger in any crisis."
units.literal: The actor-official Jing Jin and his faction fabricated, saying: "Yesterday when the royal army first rose, Jilin thought it was to attack himself and had quite a mind to refuse command; if he is not removed, should the state meet urgency, he will surely be a later trouble."

units.zh: 郭崇韜既誅，宦官愈盛，遂構成其罪，謂莊宗曰：「崇韜強項於蜀，蓋與河中響應。」
units.en: After Guo Chongtao was killed the eunuchs grew bolder still and framed Jilin, telling Zhuangzong, "Chongtao's defiance in Shu was surely coordinated with Hezhong."
units.literal: After Guo Chongtao was executed, eunuchs grew ever more powerful and then fabricated his crime, saying to Emperor Zhuangzong: "Chongtao was stiff-necked in Shu—surely he was in echo with Hezhong."

units.zh: 繼麟聞之懼，將赴京師，麵訴其事。
units.en: Hearing this, Jilin was afraid and set out for the capital to plead his case in person.
units.literal: When Jilin heard it he was afraid and was about to go to the capital to plead the matter in person.

units.zh: 其部將曰：「王有大功於國，密邇京城，群小流言，何足介意。
units.en: His officers said, "Your Highness has rendered great service to the state and dwells near the capital; the gossip of petty men is not worth heeding.
units.literal: His subordinate generals said: "Your Highness has great merit to the state and dwells close to the capital; petty men's slander—what is there to mind?

units.zh: 端居奉職，讒邪自銷，不可輕行。」
units.en: Stay at your post and perform your duties faithfully; slander will fade of itself—you must not act rashly."
units.literal: Sit upright and perform your duties; slander and evil will consume themselves—do not act lightly."

units.zh: 繼麟曰：「郭公功倍於我，尚為人構陷，吾若得麵天顏，自陳肝膈，則流言者獲罪矣。」
units.en: Jilin replied, "Lord Guo's merit doubled mine, yet he was still destroyed by plotters; if I can face the emperor and lay my heart bare, the slanderers will be punished."
units.literal: Jilin said: "Lord Guo's merit was twice mine, yet he was still framed by others; if I can face the imperial countenance and lay bare my heart and entrails, then the slanderers will be punished."

units.zh: 四年正月，繼麟入覲。
units.en: In the first month of year 4 he went to court.
units.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Jilin entered for audience.

units.zh: 景進謂莊宗曰：「河中人有告變者，言繼麟與崇韜謀叛，聞崇韜死，又與李存乂構鬆逆，當斷不斷，禍不旋踵。」
units.en: Jing Jin told Zhuangzong, "Someone from Hezhong reports that Jilin plotted rebellion with Chongtao and, after Chongtao's death, conspired with Li Cunyi; hesitation now will bring disaster at once."
units.literal: Jing Jin said to Emperor Zhuangzong: "A man from Hezhong has reported a plot, saying Jilin conspired rebellion with Chongtao; hearing Chongtao was dead, he again plotted treason with Li Cunyi; when one should cut and does not, calamity follows at the heel."

units.zh: 群閹異口同辭，莊宗駭惑不能決。
units.en: The eunuchs chorused the same accusation, and Zhuangzong, shaken and uncertain, could not decide.
units.literal: The eunuchs all spoke with one voice; Emperor Zhuangzong was alarmed and confused and could not decide.

units.zh: 是月二十三日，授繼麟滑州節度使。
units.en: On the twenty-third of that month he was appointed military governor of Huazhou.
units.literal: On the twenty-third day of that month Jilin was appointed military governor of Huazhou.

units.zh: 是夜，令朱守殷以兵圍其第，擒之，誅於徽安門外；
units.en: That night Zhu Shouyin surrounded his residence with troops, seized him, and executed him outside the Hui'an Gate;
units.literal: That night he ordered Zhu Shouyin to surround his residence with troops, seize him, and execute him outside the Hui'an Gate;

units.zh: 詔繼岌誅令德於遂州，王思同誅令錫於許州，
units.en: he ordered Jiji to execute Lingde at Suizhou and Wang Sitong to execute Lingxi at Xu Prefecture,
units.literal: he decreed that Jiji execute Lingde at Suizhou and Wang Sitong execute Lingxi at Xu Prefecture,

units.zh: 〈（吳縝《篡誤》云：《史彥瓊傳》，友謙有子建徽被殺。
units.en: (According to Wu Zhen's Compendium of Errors (Zuanwu), the Biography of Shi Yanqiong records that Youqian's son Jianhui was killed,
units.literal: (Wu Zhen's Compendium of Errors (Zuanwu) says: In the Biography of Shi Yanqiong, Youqian had a son Jianhui who was killed.

units.zh: 傳中未載。）〉
units.en: though this is not recorded in the main biography.)〉
units.literal: but this is not recorded in the biography.)〉

units.zh: 命夏魯奇誅其族於河中。
units.en: He ordered Xia Luqi to exterminate his clan at Hezhong.
units.literal: He ordered Xia Luqi to exterminate his clan at Hezhong.

units.zh: 初，魯奇至，友謙妻張氏率其家屬二百餘口見魯奇曰：「請疏骨肉名字，無致他人橫死。」
units.en: When Luqi arrived, Lady Zhang led more than two hundred family members to meet him and said, "Please list our kin by name so that no innocent may die by mistake."
units.literal: When Luqi first arrived, Youqian's wife Lady Zhang led more than two hundred members of the family to see Luqi and said: "I beg you to list the names of our kin by blood, that others may not die unjustly."

units.zh: 將刑，張氏持先賜鐵券授魯奇曰：「皇帝所賜也。」
units.en: As the execution was about to begin, Lady Zhang produced the iron certificate the emperor had granted and said, "This was bestowed by the emperor himself."
units.literal: As execution was about to take place, Lady Zhang held out the iron certificate previously bestowed and gave it to Luqi, saying: "This was granted by the emperor."

units.zh: 是時，百口塗地，冤酷之聲，行路流涕。
units.en: A hundred lives were destroyed; the cries of injustice moved every passerby to tears.
units.literal: At that time a hundred mouths were smeared on the ground; the sound of cruel injustice made passersby on the road weep.

units.zh: 先是，河中衙城閽者夜見婦人數十，袨服靚妝，仆馬炫耀，自外馳騁，笑語趨衙城。
units.en: Earlier, the yamen gatekeeper had seen dozens of women at night in splendid dress and fine makeup, with dazzling retinues of servants and horses, galloping in from outside, laughing as they rushed toward the compound.
units.literal: Earlier, the gatekeeper of the Hezhong yamen city at night saw several tens of women in splendid dress and fine makeup, with servants and horses dazzling, galloping in from outside, laughing and talking as they hurried toward the yamen city.

units.zh: 閽者不知其故，不敢詰，至門排騎而入，既而扃鎖如故，復無人跡，乃知妖鬼也。
units.en: The gatekeeper dared not question them; they pushed through the gate and entered, then the locks were fastened as before and no trace of anyone remained—he knew they were spirits.
units.literal: The gatekeeper did not know the reason and did not dare question; they reached the gate, pushed aside the riders and entered; afterward the bolts were locked as before and again there were no human traces—then he knew they were demon spirits.

units.zh: 又繼麟登逍遙樓，聞哭聲四合，詰日訊之，巷無喪者，隔歲乃族誅。
units.en: Jilin also climbed the Xiaoyao Tower and heard wailing on every side; he inquired the next day but found no mourning in the lanes; a year later his whole clan was slaughtered.
units.literal: Moreover Jilin ascended the Xiaoyao Tower and heard wailing on all four sides; he questioned people the next day—no house in the lanes was in mourning; a year later the clan was exterminated.

units.zh: 及明宗即位，始下詔昭雪焉。
units.en: Only when Emperor Mingzong took the throne was an edict issued to clear their names.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong ascended the throne, he first issued an edict to clear their names.

units.zh: 史臣曰：全義一逢亂世，十領名藩，而能免梁祖之雄猜，受莊宗之厚遇，雖由恭順，亦係貨財。
units.en: The historian remarks: Quanyi lived through chaotic times and held ten famous commands, yet escaped the Liang Founder's fierce suspicion and won Emperor Zhuangzong's generous favor—deference helped, but so did his wealth.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Quanyi once met a chaotic age and ten times held famous commands, yet could escape the Founder's heroic suspicion and receive Emperor Zhuangzong's generous treatment—though through deference, it also depended on wealth.

units.zh: 《傳》所謂「貨以藩身」者，全義得之矣。
units.en: What the Commentary calls "using wealth to preserve oneself in office," Quanyi exemplified.
units.literal: What the Commentary calls "using wealth to preserve oneself in a command," Quanyi attained it.

units.zh: 友謙向背為謀，二三其德，考其行事，亦匪純臣。
units.en: Youqian shifted allegiance as strategy demanded and was inconstant in loyalty; judged by his conduct, he too was no loyal minister.
units.literal: Youqian turned his back or faced forward as strategy required; he was inconstant in virtue; examining his conduct, he too was no pure minister.

units.zh: 然全族之誅，禍斯酷矣，得非鬼神害盈，而天道惡滿乎！
units.en: Yet the slaughter of his entire clan was calamity of the cruelest kind—was it not that spirits punish excess and Heaven abhors fullness!
units.literal: Yet the extermination of the whole clan—how cruel was that calamity! Was it not that spirits harm fullness and the Way of Heaven hates excess!

units.zh: 光啟元年，蔡賊秦宗權遣將孫儒來攻，罕之對壘數月，以兵少備竭，委城而遁，西保於澠池。
units.en: Guangqi 1 Sun Ru besieged Luoyang; outnumbered, Hanzhi fled to Mianchi.
units.literal: In Guangqi year 1, Cai bandit Qin Zongquan sent general Sun Ru to attack; Hanzhi faced the camp several months; because soldiers were few and stores exhausted, he abandoned the city and fled, west guarding at Mianchi.
